Hello from Uruguay! 🇺🇾🚀

We are Wall-ES, a team of students from Santa Elena School in Uruguay, excited to participate in the NASA Space Apps Challenge! 🌎✨
summary: Abandoned But Not Forgotten is a research project about the NASA robots and spacecraft that made history, even though most of them are no longer active. We studied nine missions: the Mars rovers Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity; the Viking 1 and InSight landers; the Ingenuity helicopter; the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle; and the deep-space probes Pioneer 10 and Voyager 1. For each one, we explained what it was designed to do, what it discovered, and how its mission ended, whether by dust storms, damaged parts, lost communication or simply traveling too far away. Our project shows that these machines are not just “space junk”: their discoveries, like evidence of ancient water on Mars or the first flight on another planet, are still used by scientists today. We want to honor them and remind people that every mission, even one that ends, opens the door to new exploration.
details:
What it does. Our presentation tells the story of nine historic NASA spacecraft, in order to show how space exploration has grown step by step:

  1. Viking 1 (1976): landed on Mars, sent photos from the surface and searched for signs of life.
  2. Lunar Roving Vehicle, Apollo 15 (1971): an electric car that let astronauts travel farther across the Moon; it was left there after the mission.
  3. Pioneer 10 (1972): the first spacecraft to cross the asteroid belt and explore Jupiter; its last signal arrived in 2003.
  4. Voyager 1 (1977): explored Jupiter and Saturn, carries the Golden Record, and is still sending data from interstellar space.
  5. Sojourner (1997): one of the first robots to drive on another planet.
  6. Spirit and Opportunity (2004): twin rovers that found evidence of ancient water on Mars; Opportunity worked for almost 15 years until a dust storm covered its solar panels.
  7. InSight (2018): studied the inside of Mars and recorded marsquakes until dust ended its mission in 2022.
  8. Ingenuity (2021): the first aircraft to make a powered flight on another planet, completing 72 flights instead of the planned five.

Benefits and intended impact. The project helps students understand that space exploration is a long story built mission by mission, and that “failure” or the end of a mission is also part of science. It inspires curiosity about the machines humans have left across the Solar System.

Tools used. Research using NASA information, and Canva for the presentation.

Creativity. We chose an emotional angle: instead of only celebrating new missions, we paid tribute to the “abandoned” robots and spacecraft and showed why they are not forgotten.

Factors we considered. Choosing missions from different places (Moon, Mars and deep space) and different decades, explaining each one in simple language, and showing both what each machine achieved and why its mission ended.
